mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined for three consecutive weeks (-13.3 to -17.9), indicating a persistent negative momentum trend. Absent any reversing signal, this trend is expected to continue, producing a lower mean over the next 4 weeks relative to the last 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell each week from -13.3 to -17.9 over the snapshot
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the mean over the last 28 days despite the observed three-week decline.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has remained deeply suppressed (-21 to -25) across all four weeks, suggesting continued constrained movement to commercial districts. This sustained transit weakness is predicted to keep RETAIL_REC depressed over the coming 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT ranged -21.3 to -24.6 with no recovery trend
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days relative to the last 28 days even though TRANSIT remains below -20 throughout.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has collapsed sharply from 26.1 to 4.6 over the last two weeks, consistent with a seasonal shift (autumn onset in Melbourne) reducing outdoor leisure activity. If this outdoor-to-indoor substitution does not redirect to retail venues, RETAIL_REC will fail to recover and may decline further.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below 10 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 4 weeks despite PARKS remaining below 10 for the trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has stayed persistently elevated (3.4 to 4.1) across all four weeks, indicating households continue spending more time at home. This sustained residential-bias behavior is expected to suppress discretionary retail and recreation trips over the next 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed in a narrow 3.4-4.1 band for four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL remains at or above 3.4 throughout the period.

Absent this crossing, no rebound signal is confirmed.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -5 points for at least one week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES ranged -8.6 to -10.6 over the snapshot period
failure_condition: WORKPLACES crosses above -5 but RETAIL_REC does not increase in the following 2 weeks.

When these three move together in this configuration, RETAIL_REC tends to weaken further as discretionary trips are deprioritized.

evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 10.6 to 4.6 and TRANSIT fell from -24.6 to -22.4 is marginal but GROCERY_PHARM rose from 9.3 to 9.6 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 2 weeks despite simultaneous declines in TRANSIT and PARKS with stable/rising GROCERY_PHARM.

mechanism_narrative: Victoria's gradual relaxation of pandemic restrictions through early 2022 is the backdrop regime; under this reopening regime, a simultaneous stabilization of WORKPLACES (narrow -8.6 to -10.6 band) and persistent negative TRANSIT indicates restrictions are not meaningfully loosening further in the short term, which combined with retail's own downtrend implies continued softness in RETAIL_REC rather than a policy-driven rebound.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both show no sustained improvement across the four weeks
regime_hint: stalled reopening under residual policy caution
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds upward over the next 4 weeks despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining flat or negative.
